correctness.rationale: Difference of the defining floor-square recurrence at n and n−1 uses floor(k)^2−floor(k−1)^2=2k−1 exactly for a divisor jump, yielding s*g=g−u+δ with g(m)=2m−1 and s(1)=g(1)=1. Mod2, g=u, so Dirichlet inversion gives s(n)≡μ(n) mod2; nonsquarefree outputs are even. For n squarefree with r prime factors, restriction of divisor convolution to the nilpotent Boolean ring R=Z[z_i]/(z_i²) gives S=1−(1−E^-1)/(2HE^-1−1). With T=∏(1+(p_i−1)z_i), the coefficient of z_A in (2T−1)^-1 is (∏_{i∈A}(p_i−1))t_|A|, t_j=Σ_{k=1}^j(-2)^k k! S(j,k)=2(-1)^jF_j from EGF 1/(2e^z−1)=2/(2−e^-z)−1. Taking the full squarefree coefficient proves s(n)=(-1)^r[1+2Σ_{j=1}^{r−1}F_j e_j(p_i−1)] for all squarefree n>1, and |s(n)|>1 for r≥2. Together with nonsquarefree parity this proves s(n)=−1 iff n is prime. Independently computed the ORIGINAL floor recurrence to n=1500, checked the ordered Bell squarefree formula at 914 squarefree n and parity at 585 nonsquarefree n; finite checks supplement the universal convolution argument.

value.rationale: The recently proposed generalized Möbius recurrence motivates evaluating a fixed substantive nonlinear function f(m)=m². The exact squarefree spectrum in ordered Bell numbers and elementary symmetric polynomials is a natural invariant linking Dirichlet convolution to ordered set partitions, and distinguishes prime factors individually; nonsquarefree parity completes a sharp theoretical prime indicator. This is far more than the elementary fact s(p)=−1 or a computational primality shortcut. The source’s all-f primality assertion cannot be applied mechanically because f≡1 is a known counterexample.
